title: Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC) vs. Clean Bench

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: A Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC) protects the worker, the environment, and (for Class II) the sample from contamination via HEPA-filtered, directional airflow. A laminar flow 'clean bench' protects only the product/sample from contamination — it is not designed to protect the worker and is not appropriate for infectious materials.
explanation: The physical resemblance between a BSC and a clean bench causes real confusion in teaching labs. A horizontal or vertical laminar flow clean bench blows HEPA-filtered air outward toward the worker to keep the work surface particulate-free (useful for sterile plant tissue culture or electronics work, for example) — that same airflow direction is precisely why it must never be used for infectious agents. A Class II BSC instead draws air inward and exhausts it through HEPA filtration, protecting the worker.

comparison.left: BSC (Class II): inward and HEPA-filtered, protecting the worker
comparison.right: Clean bench: outward toward the worker, protecting only the product

comparison.left: Yes, appropriate to its class rating
comparison.right: No — never appropriate for infectious materials

commonMisconceptions: Assuming any cabinet with a glass shield and blowing air is a 'safety cabinet' — appearance alone does not indicate worker protection.
